prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001 – “Time for Common Sense” (summary)

Core vision: Trust people over government; restore common sense by cutting taxes and bureaucracy, strengthening families and communities, raising standards in public services through choice and freedom, protecting national independence, and renewing democracy.

Families and education:
- Tax relief targeted at families: restore a Married Couple’s Allowance (worth up to £1,000), add £200 to the Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s, make Widowed Parent benefits tax‑free, reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid to the caring parent, and offer “Family Scholarships” for parents returning to work.
- Free Schools: give heads/governors full control; cut red tape; allow discipline (easy exclusion of disruptors; Progress Centres).
- Expand successful schools; allow new faith/parent/charity/company schools; Parent’s Guarantee to trigger Ofsted and management change.
- Students: no top‑up fees; raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000; endow universities to secure independence.

Law and order:
- More police; slash paperwork; “cops in shops”; parish constables.
- Tough approach to persistent young offenders; expand Secure Training Centres; link release to behaviour/qualifications.
- Mandatory jail for dealers selling to under‑16s; tougher action near schools.
- Honest sentencing (end automatic early release); prison work schemes; lifetime supervision possible for sex offenders; protect children online.
- Victims’ rights: single named contacts; reasons required for dropped/reduced charges; reform self-defence and double jeopardy law.

Economy and tax:
- Keep spending growth within trend growth; save £8bn versus Labour plans and return it in targeted tax cuts.
- Tax cuts include: abolish taxes on savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; cut petrol/diesel duty by at least 6p; business rates cuts; abolish IR35; relief for approved share options; regeneration tax breaks.
- Simpler, transparent taxes: taxpayer statements; National Accounts Commission; capital gains simplification; regulatory budgets to cut red tape yearly; new Deregulation Commission.
- Keep the pound; strengthen BoE MPC independence; Council of Economic Advisers.

Health/NHS:
- Match NHS funding plans but end political micromanagement.
- Replace Waiting List Initiative with Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits by clinical need (start with cancer/cardiac), with choice of NHS or private provision paid by NHS.
- Restore authority to ward sisters; bring back matrons; expand practice nurse roles; standalone surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; fair hospice funding.
- End tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

Older people:
- Raise basic state pension (extra for over‑75s); option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence into pension tax‑free.
- Remove 1 million pensioners from tax via higher age allowance; abolish compulsory annuity purchase at 75; consult on funded pension option for younger workers; protect assets for long-term care via pre‑funding.

Europe, defence, asylum:
- In Europe, not run by Europe: keep veto, keep pound, renegotiate Nice, insert domestic “reserved powers,” oppose EU army outside NATO.
- Support armed forces, end ECHR applicability to forces operations like other nations; back US missile defence; maintain independent nuclear deterrent.
- Asylum: secure reception centres for new applicants, fast decisions, safe‑country rule, new Removals Agency.

Welfare and civil society:
- Create Office of Civil Society; abolish charities’ irrecoverable VAT (funded by euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with “Britain Works,” paying providers for jobs secured and sustained; Can Work, Must Work Guarantee.
- Better support for disabled people: align savings rules with pensioners; new agency to pay Incapacity Benefit and fund rehab aids; tough anti‑fraud taskforce and NI number clean‑up.

Town, country, transport, environment:
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; honest food labelling; less gold‑plating of EU rules.
- Help rural services (rate cuts for shops/pubs/garages/post offices), benefit card to sustain post offices, abolish top‑down housebuilding targets, create “Blue Belts.”
- Urban Regeneration Companies; tackle antisocial tenants; expand right‑to‑buy, rent‑to‑mortgage, homesteading.
- Transport: long‑term roads/public transport plan; Road Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; cut fuel duty 6p; Brit Disc for foreign lorries; revive rail; support London Underground modernisation with no‑strike deal.
- Meet climate commitments via trading, efficiency, renewables; abolish Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear.

Culture, media, sport:
- Privatise Channel 4; use proceeds plus Lottery surpluses to endow arts (£3bn); simplify Lottery rules; back tourism.
- Single media/communications regulator; modernise ownership rules; fair BBC oversight; open access for religious broadcasters.
- Protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; streamline sports funding.

Democracy:
- Empower best “free councils”; local referendums for big tax rises; scrap English regional bodies; return powers to counties/unitaries.
- English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and pursue a substantial elected element; tougher PM/ministerial scrutiny; reduce MPs, ministers, and spin doctors.
